headline_marked: [[51 years since Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's assassination]] by renegade soldiers on August 15, 1975
headline: 51 years since Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's assassination by renegade soldiers on August 15, 1975
summary: On this day in 1975, Bangladesh's founding father and most of his family were brutally killed at his Dhanmondi residence. The nation remembers the tragic event and its profound impact.
details: Today marks the 51st death anniversary of Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. On August 15, 1975, a group of renegade army personnel brutally killed him at his Dhanmondi residence, marking one of history's most heinous and brutal assassinations.

Besides Bangabandhu, his wife Begum Fazilatunnesa Mujib, three sons Sheikh Kamal, Sheikh Jamal, and infant Sheikh Russell, along with daughters-in-law Sultana Kamal and Rosy Jamal, were killed. His only brother Sheikh Abu Naser, Colonel Jamil (who rushed to save him), SB officer Siddiqur Rahman, and army personnel Syed Mahbubul Haque also lost their lives.

On the same night, another group of soldiers attacked the residence of Sheikh Fazlul Haque Moni, Bangabandhu's nephew and a youth leader, killing him and his pregnant wife Arzu Moni. Additionally, Bangabandhu's brother-in-law Abdur Rab Serniabat, his daughter Baby, son Arif Serniabat, grandson Sukanta Babu, Serniabat's elder brother's son Sajib Serniabat, and a relative Abdul Nayeem Khan were also killed.

Bangabandhu's two daughters, Sheikh Hasina and Sheikh Rehana, survived as they were in Brussels, Belgium, at the time. Twenty-one years after the assassination, the Awami League came to power in 1996 under Sheikh Hasina's leadership, initiating the trial of the killers.

On November 8, 1998, a court sentenced 15 individuals to death in the Bangabandhu murder case, with the High Court later upholding the death sentences of 12 accused. So far, six convicts have been executed, one died abroad, and five remain fugitives.

The Awami League returned to power in 2009 under Sheikh Hasina, maintaining continuous rule for nearly 15 and a half years. During this period, the party observed month-long programs around August 15 and the August 21 grenade attack, including paying respects at Bangabandhu's portrait in Dhanmondi 32 and his grave in Tungipara.

However, following the mass uprising in July 2024, which led to the fall of Sheikh Hasina's 15-year rule, the public holiday for Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's death anniversary was cancelled last year. On August 5, 2024, during the uprising, Bangabandhu's Dhanmondi 32 residence was vandalized and set on fire, and six months later, it was attacked a second time and demolished.

In the late 1960s, despite many well-known politicians, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's leadership qualities propelled him to the forefront. Through a long struggle based on nationalist politics, he became the undisputed leader of Bangladesh's independence movement.

His historic speech on March 7, 1971, at the then Ramna Race Course Maidan (now Suhrawardy Udyan), served as an inspiration for freedom fighters during the war. Addressing millions, he declared, "This time the struggle is for our emancipation, this time the struggle is for independence."

headline_marked: [[7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes Eastern Indonesia]], triggers tsunami warning
headline: 7.7 magnitude earthquake strikes Eastern Indonesia, triggers tsunami warning
summary: A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck Indonesia's Flores region, prompting a tsunami warning and causing residents to evacuate. Initial reports indicate building damage but no casualties.
details: A powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck Eastern Indonesia's Flores region early Saturday morning, triggering a tsunami warning. Residents in affected areas have moved to higher ground amidst fears of large waves.

The earthquake, which occurred at 5:58 AM local time, had a shallow depth of just 10 kilometers. Its epicenter was located 68 kilometers northwest of Ende city in East Nusa Tenggara province, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).
Two aftershocks, including one measuring 6.1 magnitude, were felt. While there are no immediate reports of casualties, several buildings have sustained damage, with cracks appearing in walls.

Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) issued the tsunami warning, urging residents to stay away from beaches and riverbanks. They warned of potential waves between 0.5 and 3 meters high in East Nusa Tenggara, South Sulawesi, and West Nusa Tenggara provinces.
In Maumere city on Flores Island, residents began evacuating to higher areas. A local correspondent observed the sea water receding, a phenomenon often seen before a tsunami.

Indonesian television footage showed damaged buildings, and hundreds were seen evacuating to safe locations in the nearby Nagekeo Regency. Authorities have detected tsunami waves between 19 and 30 centimeters high.

Indonesia is highly prone to earthquakes and volcanic eruptions due to its location on the Pacific "Ring of Fire." The archipelago, comprising over 17,000 islands, is one of the world's most seismically active regions.
Meanwhile, Australia's Tsunami Warning Centre confirmed that there is no tsunami threat to Australia's mainland or territories from this earthquake.
